prompt: Hypothetical. Best bid Rs 249.90, best ask Rs 250.10. What is the spread in rupees?
Hypothetical. Same prices: best bid Rs 249.90, best ask Rs 250.10. You buy 100 shares at the market. What is the cost above the mid-price in rupees?
solution: Mid-price = (249.90 plus 250.10) divided by 2 = Rs 250.00. Cost above mid = (250.10 minus 250.00) multiplied by 100 = Rs 10. Check: 100 shares at Rs 250.10 cost Rs 25,010, and 100 shares at Rs 250.00 cost Rs 25,000. The difference is Rs 10.

options.text: A fee that the broker charges
The best ask minus the best bid
The best bid plus the best ask
The volume multiplied by the price

explanations.a: The spread is not a fee. It is the gap between the best bid and the best ask. Broker charges are shown separately.
explanations.c: Adding the bid and the ask gives a number that is used for the mid-price, not the spread.
explanations.d: Volume multiplied by price gives traded value. It is not the spread.

prompt: Hypothetical. A very large bid quantity appears at Rs 249.90. A trader thinks the price will hold at that level. What is the best reply?

options.text: Correct. A big bid guarantees that the price will hold.
The bid is one moment in the order book. It can change or disappear, so it does not promise support.
Correct, because large quantities always stay in place.
Wrong. A bid can never be large.

explanations.a: No bid guarantees a price. Orders can be cancelled at any time.
explanations.c: Large quantities can be cancelled or filled at any moment, so they do not always stay.
explanations.d: Bids can be large. The issue is that they change, not that they cannot be large.

prompt: Spot the mistake. A student writes: 'The depth shows a big bid, so I can use it to plan my end-of-day exit.' Which part is the mistake?

options.text: The depth shows a big bid.
So I can use it to plan my end-of-day exit.

explanations.a: This describes what the screen shows at one moment. It is not the mistake, although the bid can change.
explanations.b: Depth shows one moment and can change quickly. It is not a basis for an end-of-day plan.

prompt: Hypothetical. Best bid Rs 180.40, best ask Rs 180.60, mid-price Rs 180.50. You buy 200 shares at the market. What is the cost above mid in rupees?
solution: Cost above mid = (180.60 minus 180.50) multiplied by 200 = Rs 20. Check: 200 shares at Rs 180.60 cost Rs 36,120, and 200 shares at Rs 180.50 cost Rs 36,100. The difference is Rs 20.
